newsitem.title: USA: Consumer confidence holds at six-year high.
newsitem.headline: Consumer confidence holds at six-year high.

text.p: Consumer confidence in the economy held steady at a six-year high in September, a private research group said Tuesday, and the optimism is expected to extend into the holiday season.
The Conference Board said its index of consumer confidence was at 111.8 in September, little changed from a revised reading of 112.0 in August.
The New York-based private research business group said its expectations component index rose in September to 100.4 from a revised 100.3 in the previous month.
The survey showed consumers are "quite optimistic about the next six months," said Lynn Franco, associate director of the board's Consumer Research Centre.
"With consumers in high spirits, the outlook for holiday spending appears to be bright," she said.
"After remaining flat over the last year, consumer confidence broke out in July and is currently holding at a six-year high," Franco said.

The Consumer Confidence Survey, which is based on a sampling of 5,000 households, found that the proportion of respondents who felt that jobs are "hard to get" dropped to 21 percent in September from 22 percent in August.
About 27 percent of consumers say business conditions are "good," off moderately from 28.5 percent in August.
The group said the percentage of respondents who expect business conditions to improve moved up to 17.3 percent from 16.1 percent.

In addition to posting the national measures, the survey showed that regional confidence improved dramatically in New England, having jumped by 24 percent over the past three months. Confidence levels there had been "in the doldrums since early 1990," the Board said.

The East South Central region -- including Kentucky, Tennessee, Alabama and Mississippi -- was the only area to report a decline in confidence over the past three months, dropping about 1.0 percent, it said.
